        "contents": "        if currentDistance &lt;= autoStopDistanceThreshold &amp;&amp; initialDist &gt; autoStopDistanceThreshold {\n            // Devices have moved close to each other, stop navigation automatically\n            // Mark navigation as stopped to prevent re-triggering\n            navigationStopped = true\n            // Show info overlay and trigger haptics\n            Haptic.notifySuccess()\n            infoOverlayManager.show(\n                message: NSLocalizedString(\"navigation_stopped_automatically\", comment: \"Navigation stopped automatically - devices are close\"),\n                duration: 6.0,\n                animationsAllowed: animationsAllowed\n            )\n            // Stop navigation but keep the map view showing both devices\n            stopNavigation()\n        }\n    }\n    \n    private func stopNavigation() {\n        // Stop navigation without dismissing the view\n        // Clear route and navigation info, but keep the map showing both devices\n        route = nil\n        travelTime = nil\n        distanceText = nil\n        navigationOverlayViewModel = nil\n        lastOverlayStepIndex = nil\n        routeInfoState.hide()\n        stopAutoUpdate()\n        showChromeIfNeeded()\n        // Disable navigation modes when navigation is stopped\n        isNavigationMode = false\n        isFollowDeviceHeadingMode = false\n        shouldPerformInitialNavigationZoom = false\n        // Reset follow camera state\n        lastFollowCameraUpdate = nil\n        lastFollowCameraCenter = nil\n        lastFollowCameraHeading = nil\n        followCameraDistanceOverride = nil\n        isFollowAutoZoomEnabled = true\n        isAutoCenteringEnabled = true\n        // Update bottom accessory to reflect that navigation is stopped\n        updateBottomAccessory()\n    }\n}\n\n// MARK: - Distance Formatting\nextension iPhone_DeviceNavigationView {\n    /// Attempts to reuse a previously calculated route if the movement since that",

      "codeBlock": {

        "contents": "---\nname: Turn Feedback Cues\noverview: Add turn-by-turn haptic and sound feedback during reversed-route navigation mode, using NavigationOverlayKit symbols and the existing sound player so system silent mode is respected.\ntodos:\n  - id: bind-symbol-feedback\n    content: Bind NavigationOverlayViewModel.$symbol to feedback\n    status: completed\n  - id: add-haptic-helpers\n    content: Expose light/heavy haptic helpers in Haptics\n    status: completed\n  - id: map-symbols-to-feedback\n    content: Map NavigationInstruction.Symbol to left/right/straight cues\n    status: completed\nisProject: false\n---\n\n# Turn Feedback Cues Plan\n\n## Scope and assumptions\n\n- Feedback should only fire when the route is reversed and navigation mode is ON (double-tap enabled).\n- We will map NavigationOverlayKit symbols to left/right/straight and use the existing &#96;SoundEffectPlayer&#96; so silent mode is respected.\n- Sound file defaults (can be renamed later): &#96;nav_left.caf&#96;, &#96;nav_right.caf&#96;, &#96;nav_straight.caf&#96; under &#96;miataru/Assets/sounds/&#96;.\n\n## Approach\n\n- Bind to &#96;NavigationOverlayViewModel.$symbol&#96; with Combine and trigger feedback when the symbol changes.\n- Gate feedback so it only fires when &#96;isRouteReversed &amp;&amp; isNavigationMode &amp;&amp; isViewActive&#96;.\n- Add public haptic helpers for light/heavy impacts to differentiate left/right/straight.\n\n## Files to update\n\n- &#96;[/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/Devices%20Views/iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift)&#96;\n  - Add feedback sound name constants.\n  - Add a Combine subscription to &#96;viewModel.$symbol&#96; and store in &#96;cancellables&#96;.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

to cues:\n    - Left: &#96;.slightLeft&#96;, &#96;.left&#96;, &#96;.sharpLeft&#96;, &#96;.uTurn&#96;\n    - Right: &#96;.slightRight&#96;, &#96;.right&#96;, &#96;.sharpRight&#96;\n    - Straight: &#96;.straight&#96;, &#96;.start&#96;, &#96;.arrive&#96;, &#96;.cross&#96;, &#96;.tunnel&#96;, &#96;.bridge&#96;, &#96;.stairs&#96;, &#96;.escalator&#96;\n  - Use &#96;SoundEffectPlayer.shared.play(named:fileExtension:)&#96;         "contents": "    private func formattedDistance(_ meters: CLLocationDistance) -&gt; String {\n        let usesMetric: Bool\n        if #available(iOS 16.0, *) {\n            usesMetric = Locale.current.measurementSystem == .metric\n        } else {\n            usesMetric = Locale.current.usesMetricSystem\n        }\n        let value: Double\n        let unit: UnitLength\n        if usesMetric {\n            value = meters / 1000.0\n            unit = .kilometers\n        } else {\n            value = meters / 1609.344\n            unit = .miles\n        }\n        let measurement = Measurement(value: value, unit: unit)\n        let formatter = MeasurementFormatter()\n        formatter.locale = .current\n        formatter.unitStyle = .short\n        formatter.unitOptions = .providedUnit\n        let numberFormatter = NumberFormatter()\n        numberFormatter.maximumFractionDigits = 0\n        numberFormatter.minimumFractionDigits = 0\n        formatter.numberFormatter = numberFormatter\n        return formatter.string(from: measurement)\n    }\n\n    private func transportSymbolName() -&gt; String {\n        switch settings.navigationTransportType {\n        case 0: return \"figure.walk\"\n        case 2: return \"car\"\n        case 3: return \"tram\"\n        default: return \"car\"\n        }\n    }\n\n    private enum NavigationFeedbackDirection {\n        case left\n        case right\n        case straight\n    }\n\n    private enum NavigationHapticStyle {\n        case light\n        case medium\n        case heavy\n    }\n\n    private func bindNavigationOverlayFeedback(to viewModel: NavigationOverlayViewModel) {\n        navigationOverlayCancellables.removeAll()\n        viewModel.$symbol\n            .compactMap { $0 }\n            .removeDuplicates()\n            .sink { symbol in\n                guard isViewActive, !isRouteFromDeviceToUser, isNavigationMode else { return }\n                playNavigationFeedback(for: symbol)\n            }\n            .store(in: &amp;navigationOverlayCancellables)\n    }\n\n    private func playNavigationFeedback(for symbol: NavigationInstruction.Symbol) {\n        let direction = navigationFeedbackDirection(for: symbol)",

        "contents": "    private func calculateRoute(ignoreCache: Bool = false, retryAttempt: Int = 0) {\n        // Calculate a new route between user and selected device.\n        // Prefers a cached route when movement &lt; 100m; applies a daily network request limit.\n        guard let user = userCoordinate, let device = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        if retryAttempt == 0 {\n            routeRetryTask?.cancel()\n            routeRetryTask = nil\n            pendingRouteRetryOnReconnect = false\n        }\n        // Try to reuse cached route first unless explicitly told to ignore cache\n        if !ignoreCache {\n            if useCachedRouteIfValid() { return }\n            // Only recalc when one of the positions changed since the last route calculation (or if there's no route yet)\n            let userTimestampChanged = userTimestamp != lastRouteUserTimestamp\n            let deviceTimestampChanged = deviceTimestamp != lastRouteDeviceTimestamp\n            var userCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastUser = lastRouteUserCoordinate {\n                userCoordinatesChanged = (lastUser.latitude != user.latitude) || (lastUser.longitude != user.longitude)\n            }\n            var deviceCoordinatesChanged = true\n            if let lastDevice = lastRouteDeviceCoordinate {\n                deviceCoordinatesChanged = (lastDevice.latitude != device.latitude) || (lastDevice.longitude != device.longitude)\n            }\n            let transportTypeChanged = settings.navigationTransportType != lastRouteTransportType\n            let shouldRecalculate = (route == nil) || userTimestampChanged || deviceTimestampChanged || userCoordinatesChanged || deviceCoordinatesChanged || transportTypeChanged\n            if !shouldRecalculate { return }\n        }\n\n        // Enforce daily limit through centralized counter with calendar-day reset\n        routeCounter.checkAndResetIfNeeded()\n        guard routeCounter.count &lt; routeRequestDailyLimit else {\n            showErrorOverlay(\n                \"Daily route request limit reached\",",

      "codeBlock": {

          "endPosition": {
            "line": 152
          }
        },
        "contents": "**For developers:**\n- &#96;LocationManager&#96; posts &#96;didSendOwnLocationUpdate&#96; notifications; &#96;ErrorOverlayManager&#96; and &#96;ErrorOverlay&#96; provide reusable alert UIs, and map views toggle a network icon via &#96;showNetworkErrorIcon&#96; flags.\n- Status is presented as a dedicated page; related counters (e.g., daily route requests) are maintained in settings/state for diagnostics.\n\n## Caching and Reverse Geocoding\n**For users:**\n- Device list rows display last seen time, distance, and approximate place name without requiring a network connection every time.\n- Cached data is also used by device and group maps so known positions remain visible offline until refreshed.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&#96; caches coordinates, manages a centralized reverse‑geocoding queue with a configurable distance threshold, and stores results in &#96;Application Support&#96;. Views consult the cache first before hitting the network and throttle UI updates to the configured map update interval.\n- Own‑device updates trigger immediate cache writes to kick off reverse geocoding promptly. A &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96; caches routes by device and transport, with distance‑based invalidation.\n- Static map elements such as &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and &#96;DeviceNameLabel&#96; are rasterized and cached with keys that include color scheme and display scale; renderers respect Dynamic Type and set &#96;isOpaque=false&#96; where appropriate.\n\n## Haptic Feedback and UI Enhancements\n**For users:**\n- Actions like successful refresh trigger subtle haptic feedback, pulsing accuracy circles show location precision, and shimmering indicators highlight loading states.\n\n- Animations for pulsing/shimmer are automatically reduced in Low Power Mode or when the app is backgrounded to save energy.\n\n**For developers:**\n- The &#96;Haptic&#96; utility abstracts platform differences. Shared UI elements such as &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96;, &#96;PulsingAccuracyCircle&#96;, &#96;Shimmer&#96;, &#96;MapCompass&#96;, and &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; reside under &#96;views/Common&#96; and are reused across device and group map views.\n\n## Multi‑platform Support\n**For users:**",

        "contents": "        }\n        return false\n    }\n\n    private func openInAppleMaps() {\n        // Open the route in the Apple Maps app using the selected transport type\n        guard let dest = deviceCoordinate else { return }\n        let source: MKMapItem\n        let destination: MKMapItem\n        // Non-reversed (device→user): open device→user. Reversed (user→device): open user→device.\n        if isRouteFromDeviceToUser {\n            source = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: dest))\n            source.name = device.DeviceName.isEmpty ? device.DeviceID : device.DeviceName\n            destination = MKMapItem.forCurrentLocation()\n        } else {\n            source = MKMapItem.forCurrentLocation()\n            destination = MKMapItem(placemark: MKPlacemark(coordinate: dest))\n            destination.name = device.DeviceName.isEmpty ? device.DeviceID : device.DeviceName\n        }\n        var options: [String: Any] = [:]\n        switch settings.navigationTransportType {\n        case 0: options[MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeKey] = MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeWalking\n        case 3: options[MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeKey] = MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeTransit\n        default: options[MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeKey] = MKLaunchOptionsDirectionsModeDriving\n        }\n        MKMapItem.openMaps(with: [source, destination], launchOptions: options)\n    }\n\n    private func transportTypeFromSetting(_ value: Int) -&gt; MKDirectionsTransportType {\n        switch value {\n        case 0: return .walking\n        case 3: return .transit\n        default: return .automobile\n        }\n    }\n\n    private func showErrorOverlay(_ debugMessage: String, _ userMessage: String) {\n        debugLog(\"Error: \\(debugMessage)\")\n        errorOverlayManager.show(message: userMessage, animationsAllowed: animationsAllowed)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Remote updates for the selected device only\n\n    private func fetchTargetDeviceLocation(resetAndRecenter: Bool, ignoreRouteCache: Bool = false) async {\n        // Fetch latest location for just the selected device from the server.",

                  "content": "I need to implement a global setting for \"automatic route update during navigation.” The user’s request includes linking this behavior with a global setting, listing it in SettingsView, and having it default to 'on.' Kurzfassung der Prüfung und der Änderung:

---

## Befund: Haptics im Reversed-Modus (User → Zielgerät)

**Logik war inhaltlich korrekt verdrahtet:**
- Reversed = User → Gerät = `isRouteFromDeviceToUser == false`
- Haptics/Sound laufen nur, wenn `!isRouteFromDeviceToUser` und `isNavigationMode` (nach Doppel-Tap) und `isViewActive`
- `playNavigationFeedback(for:)` wird aus `bindNavigationOverlayFeedback` aufgerufen, sobald sich das aktuelle Navigationssymbol (`viewModel.$symbol`) ändert

**Bug:**  
Der Combine-`sink` in `bindNavigationOverlayFeedback` hat beim Erstellen eine **Kopie** der View (Struct) erfasst. Darin waren `isViewActive`, `isRouteFromDeviceToUser` und **`isNavigationMode`** zum Zeitpunkt der Routenberechnung gespeichert – also **vor** dem Doppel-Tap, also war `isNavigationMode` in der Closure dauerhaft `false`. Die Guard schlug deshalb weiterhin fehl, auch nach dem Doppel-Tap, und die Haptics liefen nie.

---

## Änderung (Fix)

Es gibt jetzt ein **Referenzobjekt** `NavigationFeedbackGate`, das die aktuellen Werte hält und mit der View synchron gehalten wird:

1. **`NavigationFeedbackGate`** (neue Klasse) mit `isViewActive`, `isRouteFromDeviceToUser`, `isNavigationMode`.
2. **Synchronisation:**
   - In **onAppear**: Gate mit aktuellem View-State füllen.
   - In **onDisappear**: `gate.isViewActive = false`.
   - In **onChange(of: isRouteFromDeviceToUser)**: `gate.isRouteFromDeviceToUser` aktualisieren.
   - In **onChange(of: isNavigationMode)**: `gate.isNavigationMode` aktualisieren.
3. **`bindNavigationOverlayFeedback`**: Im Sink wird nur noch das Gate ausgewertet (`gate.isViewActive`, `!gate.isRouteFromDeviceToUser`, `gate.isNavigationMode`). Da das Gate eine Referenz ist, liest der Sink damit immer den **aktuellen** Zustand, auch nach Doppel-Tap.

Damit spielen die Haptics (und Sounds) im Reversed-Modus (Navigation vom Nutzer zum Zielgerät) korrekt, sobald der Nutzer per Doppel-Tap in den Navigationsmodus geht und sich das Symbol (z. B. links/rechts) ändert.

[playing system sounds in iOS](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/15304111/playing-system-sounds-in-ios)<br/><br/># Playing System Sounds Programmatically in iOS UIKit<br/><br/>To play iOS system sounds programmatically, use the `AudioServicesPlaySystemSound()` function from the AudioToolbox framework.[1][2]<br/><br/>## Basic Implementation<br/><br/>Import AudioToolbox and call the function with a system sound ID:[1]<br/><br/>```swift<br/>import AVFoundation<br/>let systemSoundID: SystemSoundID = 1016<br/>AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(systemSoundID)<br/>```<br/><br/>Or in Objective-C:[2]<br/><br/>```objc<br/>#import <AudioToolbox/AudioServices.h><br/>AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(1103);<br/>```<br/><br/>## System Sound IDs<br/><br/>Common system sound IDs include:[2][4]<br/>- **1103** - Beep/alert sound<br/>- **1104** - Key press tock sound<br/>- **1016** - Tweet sound<br/><br/>For vibration: `AudioServicesPlaySystemSound(kSystemSoundID_Vibrate)`[2]<br/><br/>A comprehensive list of available sound IDs is available at the [iPhoneDevWiki AudioServices page](http://iphonedevwiki.net/index.php/AudioServices).[2][4] An updated list is also maintained on [GitHub](https://github.com/TUNER88/iOSSystemSoundsLibrary).[1]<br/><br/>## Requirements<br/><br/>- Add the **AudioToolbox framework** to your project[2][4]<br/>- System sounds are located at `/System/Library/Audio/UISounds/` on physical devices (not available in simulator)[1]<br/>- Note: Using undocumented sound IDs may carry app review risks, though using the AudioServices API itself is safe.[2] |

                  "content": "  \"plan\": \"# Turn Feedback Cues Plan\\n\\n## Scope and assumptions\\n- Feedback should only fire when the route is reversed and navigation mode is ON (double-tap enabled).\\n- We will map NavigationOverlayKit symbols to left/right/straight and use the existing &amp;#96;SoundEffectPlayer&amp;#96; so silent mode is respected.\\n- Sound file defaults (can be renamed later): &amp;#96;nav_left.caf&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;nav_right.caf&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;nav_straight.caf&amp;#96; under &amp;#96;miataru/Assets/sounds/&amp;#96;.\\n\\n## Approach\\n- Hook into step-change detection where navigation instructions advance and derive the symbol via &amp;#96;NavigationInstruction.from(route:currentStepIndex)&amp;#96;. The symbol already encodes slight/sharp/uturn and localized parsing.\\n- Trigger sound + haptic only when the step index changes and the view is active, scoped to reversed route + navigation mode.\\n- Add public haptic helpers for light/heavy impacts to differentiate left/right/straight.\\n\\n## Files to update\\n- &amp;#96;[/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru [... omitted end of long line]"

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>

SoundEffectPlayer uses .ambient category - that typically respects the silent switch (no sound when muted). So when nav_left/nav_right are missing, nothing plays.

I'll add support for system sounds. Options:
1. In SoundEffectPlayer: add a method like `playSystemSound(id: SystemSoundID)` that uses AudioToolbox. But system sounds often ignore silent switch - need to check.
2. In the navigation view: if the custom sound doesn't exist (or we want a fallback), call AudioServicesPlaySystemSound with 1103 (Tink) for left and 1104 (Tock) for right.

Actually the cleanest approach: add to SoundEffectPlayer a method that plays a system sound by ID, and use it only when we want "system fallback". Then in playNavigationFeedback we can: first try SoundEffectPlayer.play(named: nav_left) - if that fails (no file), the player returns silently. So we have no sound. We could either:
A) In SoundEffectPlayer.play(named:), if the resource is missing, optionally play a system sound fallback. That would require the player to know about fallback IDs per name, which is a bit coupled.

## System-Sounds für Links/Rechts

Es gibt **iOS-System-Sounds**, die sich gut für kurze „Pling“/„Beep“-Hinweise eignen. Sie sind eingebaut und respektieren die Stummschaltung.

### Umgesetzt

1. **SoundEffectPlayer**
   - **`playSystemSound(_ systemSoundID: SystemSoundID)`** – spielt einen System-Sound (AudioToolbox).
   - **`hasResource(named:fileExtension:)`** – prüft, ob eine Sound-Ressource im Bundle existiert (gleiche Suchpfade wie `play(named:fileExtension:)`).
   - Gemeinsame URL-Suche in **`soundResourceURL(for:fileExtension:)`** für `play` und `hasResource`.

2. **Navigation (Links/Rechts)**
   - **Links:** System-Sound **1103** („Tink“ – kurzer, heller Ton).
   - **Rechts:** System-Sound **1104** („Tock“ – kurzer Klick).
   - **Logik:** Wenn `nav_left.caf` bzw. `nav_right.caf` im Bundle existieren, werden diese abgespielt, sonst der jeweilige System-Sound.

### Verhalten

- **Jetzt:** Ohne eigene Dateien erklingt beim Abbiegen **Tink** (links) bzw. **Tock** (rechts) zusammen mit dem Haptic-Feedback.
- **Später:** Sobald du `nav_left.caf` und/oder `nav_right.caf` in z. B. `Assets/sounds/` oder `sounds/` legst, werden diese automatisch verwendet.

### Weitere System-Sounds (optional)

Aus der [iOS-System-Sound-Liste](https://github.com/TUNER88/iOSSystemSoundsLibrary) z. B.:

- **1057** – Tink (PINKeyPressed)
- **1105** – Tock (noch ein KeyPressed-Variant)
- **1111** – jbl_confirm.caf
- **1112** – jbl_cancel.caf

Die IDs **1103** und **1104** sind dokumentiert (KeyPressed) und klingen gut unterscheidbar für links/rechts. Wenn du andere Töne willst, können wir die IDs in den Konstanten `navigationLeftSystemSoundID` / `navigationRightSystemSoundID` anpassen.

Summary of what was committed:

---

**Commit:** `15d8e308` — **Fix reversed-route navigation haptics; add system sounds for turn feedback**

**1. Reversed-route navigation haptics**
- Turn-by-turn haptics/sounds did not run after double-tap because the Combine sink in `bindNavigationOverlayFeedback` closed over the view struct and kept `isNavigationMode == false`.
- **Fix:** Introduced `NavigationFeedbackGate` (reference type), updated in `onAppear`/`onDisappear` and in `onChange(of: isRouteFromDeviceToUser)` / `onChange(of: isNavigationMode)`. The sink now reads from the gate so it always sees the current flags; haptics and sounds run correctly in reversed navigation mode.

**2. Turn feedback sounds (left/right)**
- **SoundEffectPlayer:** `playSystemSound(_:)` (AudioToolbox), `hasResource(named:fileExtension:)`, and shared `soundResourceURL(for:fileExtension:)` for bundle lookup.
- **Navigation:** If `nav_left.caf` / `nav_right.caf` exist in the bundle they are used; otherwise system sounds **1103** (Tink) and **1104** (Tock). System sounds respect the silent switch.

**Files:** `miataru/SoundEffectPlayer.swift`, `miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift`
